title: The Seaside Hotel Turns Down the Lights

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Lie down comfortably and let the surface receive you. This practice offers deep rest while leaving sleep to do its own important work.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft distant waves lapping] Imagine a seaside hotel after midnight. Begin at the left toes, foot, ankle, calf, knee, and thigh as rooms along the west wing go dark.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft curtain fabric rustling] Feel the right toes, foot, ankle, calf, knee, and thigh. Curtains close softly along the east wing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice both legs and the pelvis. Let their weight sink like luggage finally placed on the floor.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Move through lower belly, lower back, ribs, chest, and upper back. The lift stops humming; the lobby clock keeps time alone.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel left fingers, hand, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Let every key be returned to the desk.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now right fingers, hand, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Both arms can be entirely off duty.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice throat and neck... jaw... lips... tongue... cheeks. Let the face become an unoccupied room.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the eyelids, space around the eyes, brow, forehead, temples, ears, back of the head, and scalp.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint distant surf] Hear any distant sound as surf beyond the hotel windows. It can roll in and out without requiring attention.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Sense the whole body at once, from scalp to toes. The building rests beside the ocean and breathing continues like a quiet tide.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Nothing has to feel heavy. Nothing has to disappear. Let rest be the absence of another assignment.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Remain here for several breaths while the hotel keeps its patient watch beside the dark water.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Invite movement back into hands and feet. Open your eyes slowly, as though morning has reached the curtains.
